 Move over, K-beauty; it’s all about K-wellness now, and these are the brands that have launched at Boots
 Well by Stylist 
 By Miranda Larbi 
 5 hours ago Credit: Adobe
 Credit: Adobe
 3 min read
 save for later
 Make us preferred on Google
 You don’t have to spend a fortune on serums and masks to tap into the K-beauty and wellness trends? Boots is fast becoming an emporium of all things Korean wellbeing, as these picks prove.
 The moment Korean beauty hit our shores, it revolutionised the way we look at skincare. Tired, dry skin suddenly got drenched in snail mucin and glow serum. Angry spots were covered up with fun yet effective stickers. Even the most avid sun-worshipper started investing in SPF50++ from Beauty of Joseon. We’re more obsessed with dewy, healthy skin than ever before, and we’re starting to realise that it very much starts from within.
 Wellness and beauty are two industries increasingly looking to merge, and nowhere is that more evident than at Boots. Since launching its K-beauty range, the high street retailer has seen a 76% year-on-year increase in searches for Korean beauty brands on its website. And now, it’s leaning fully into the next big trend: K-wellness.
 K-wellness is all about nutrition-based beauty: drinks to banish hangovers and fatigue, vitamin elixirs, functional foods and collegen jellies.

 From PDRN to NAD+, this is the K-beauty brand behind the latest skincare trends 
 “Launching into the K-wellness space represents a bold new era of wellness, both for Boots and the wider industry,” says Joe Thorley-Mitchell, director of Boots brand. “While the pace of innovation continues to accelerate, we’re doing the same – tapping into what we do best by bringing the latest trends straight from Seoul, at surprisingly affordable price points.
 “From chia fibre jellies to collagen cool melts and popping vitamins, we’re bringing some of Korea’s most exciting products to Boots. With dedicated wellness zones in over 30 stores and more than 500 health and wellness specialists across the UK, we’re making it easier for customers to discover the latest trends with expert support they can trust.”
 Want to tap into some of the 40 Korean brands at Boots ? Below are just a few of the wellness brands to have launched this year.
 Rin
 Sick of mixing collagen into your coffee? Wish there was a more fun way to consume skincare? Rin’s Collagen+ Jelly Sticks come in snackable pouches for on-the-go skin support, while its passion fruit glow strips are designed to deliver skin-loving liposomal glutathione without the need for water. Founded by a Korean mother-and-daughter duo, it’s all about delicious-tasting, accessible supplementation.   
 Available at Boots, £19.99 for 14 strips 
 Explore now HABI
 Habi – a Boots brand – has now formally entered the K-wellness space with five new products. Fun offerings include K-pop sherbet sticks (designed to reduce stress and aid sleep) and fibre jelly sticks (for gut health).
 Available at Boots, £10 for 30 sachets 
 Explore now Medicube 
 The next time you’ve got a big event, try Medicube’s Collagen Night Wrapping Mask the night before. Simply apply an even layer of this mask before bed, let it dry and then go to sleep. When you wake up, peel the mask off to reveal glowy, dewy skin. 
 Available at Boots, £16.11 
 Explore now BB Lab
 With over 20 million units sold last year, this supplement brand already has an army of followers. Choose between a matcha latte enzyme blend and a powder collagen designed for deep skin hydration. 
 Available at Boots, £24 for 10 sachets 
 Explore now PrePear 
 We’ve already given this hangover tool a thorough test and had some promising results. Made from 100% Shingo Korean pear juice, you simply drink a pouch before you start boozing, and you may feel more refreshed the following morning. Expect to see PrePear everywhere this festive season, but just remember that it can’t undo the effects of eight espresso martinis.
 Available at Boots, £15.50 for 6 
 Buy PrePear Seoul Bloom
 Korean skincare is all about creating healthy, radiant, resilient skin – and Seoul Bloom’s formulas support those goals. Choose from retinol-infused sour lemon sherbet, green apple-flavoured hyaluronic acid and high-strength beauty shots. 
 Available at Boots, £10 for 14 sachets 
 Explore now Youngsan 
 When you think of olive oil, your mind immediately wanders to the Med. But Korea is leading the charge when it comes to oil shots, as Youngsan’s cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil offerings prove. The brand’s all about blending Korean daily rituals with scientific benefits. Not into oil? Check out its hydrating grapefruit, kelp and pumpkin water.
 Available at Boots, £10 for 14 sachets
